newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity close lower in line with natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity close lower in line with natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower after natural gas futures were pulled down by a wave of profit taking, market sources said Tuesday.
The drop came despite sharply higher next-day cash market prices attributed to freezing weather in the Northwest.
"This market is extremely gas sensitive. More so at PV (Palo Verde) than COB (California-Oregon border)," said one futures dealer.
He and others noted that market fundamentals failed to fully support the recent run-up in electricity, but the psychological mood remains bullish.
"This market is tough to sell into, but it is feeling real top heavy," said another trader.
January COB futures settled down 6 cents a megawatt hour (MWh) at $27.25. February COB finished down 47 cents at $20.50. Other COB contracts ended 5 to 45 cents lower.
January Palo Verde futures settled down 30 cents at $28.25/MWh, while February PV finished 70 cents lower at $22.00. Other PV months finished 20 to 75 cents lower.
